blocking_focus: Complete the candidate-bound Tester MCP state matrix.

preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `native_godot_project` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

Keep frozen technical baseline `host_godot_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Repair the three host-gated release-convergence surfaces and add the required authored choice hierarchy capability with player-visible, same-loop retestable behavior while preserving the native authored world package and gameplay baseline.

diagnosis.root_cause: The release candidate has three independent integration defects: camera/arena framing hides the central landmark, authored Bellkeeper and Grave Brute meshes expose degenerate UV surfaces, and automatic attack audio lacks a verified bounded lantern-impact closure.

stop_conditions: Stop after the three bounded repairs, choice-presentation implementation, and focused code/import checks are complete; leave host recapture, formal verdicts, and issue closure to Tester/GameLoop Runtime.
Do not replace preserved authored assets or expand into deferred HUD, upgrade, performance, or other backlog gaps beyond the required choice hierarchy capability.

strategy.rationale: Use three bounded families: spatial binding/collision restoration with explicit occluder isolation; authored visual/resource binding repair extended to the required upgrade-choice hierarchy; and isolated automatic-combat audio causality. Cover every required gap exactly once and partition every active issue exactly once.

code: Parse and lint every modified GDScript/resource file; run native project boot/import checks for affected scenes and resources.

Run focused mesh validation for Bellkeeper and Grave Brute, spatial bounds/collision checks for the authored arena and central landmark, upgrade-card scene/input-map checks, and audio source-event/routing checks for SEMI and quick AUTO.
runtime: Tester/GameLoop Runtime recaptures the required MCP state matrix for spawn, ordinary movement/movement replay, dash, landmark visibility, collision, boundary, mesh render, upgrade-choice focus/value states, SEMI, AUTO, hit/miss, and lifecycle reset, then performs formal gap verdicts and active-issue closure.
Tester isolates mixed-output stems, verifies one bounded transient per attack, validates no duplicate generic VFX replay, and checks lifecycle reset.
visual: Capture sparse gameplay views for spawn, critical route, central building/landmark cardinal views, perimeter/boundary, Bellkeeper/Grave Brute renders, and the level-up choice page; compare same framing on retest.

Inspect SEMI/AUTO adjacent event-window frames for readable attack/impact VFX, ensure the central landmark does not disappear or become occluded during ordinary traversal, and verify silhouettes/icons and focus states remain legible.

done_when: The arena presents a larger traversable scale with a coherent external world/external depth around the playable court.
The central building/landmark remains visible from spawn, critical route, and cardinal traversal views without disappearance or camera occlusion drift.
The central landmark and perimeter have aligned collision; ordinary movement/movement replay cannot pass through the building or leave the playable boundary.
Spawn, objective anchors, navigation, and camera framing are bound to native authored streets/terrain, with proxy/support clutter minimized or removed.
Focused candidate checks pass for project boot/import, affected scene loading, spatial bounds/collision, and deterministic Tester setup hooks.
tasks.instructions: Repair the arena/map integration as one spatial root-cause cluster. Use a materially different approach from prior transform tuning: audit and restore the direct authored-instance, wrapper, collision, navigation, spawn, and camera bindings, then explicitly isolate only the occluder volumes that cross the sight lane. Expand to a larger traversable scale with a coherent external world and external depth while keeping native streets, buildings, props, materials, and the central landmark authoritative. Ensure the central building/landmark and perimeter collision agree in one transform space and remain stable under ordinary movement/movement replay, with no disappearance or occlusion drift. Do not replace, split, duplicate, hide, or surgically edit the preserved authored package. Leave deterministic spawn, critical-route, cardinal-view, landmark-collision, and boundary states for Tester recapture.
tasks.title: Restore arena scale, landmark visibility, and collision

done_when: Bellkeeper and Grave Brute runtime-visible meshes load with valid, non-degenerate UV surfaces and retain authored materials/textures and scale.
Mesh validation reports no degenerate UV warnings for repaired instances, and no import/runtime errors are introduced.
The repaired enemies remain correctly placed, lit, and readable in representative gameplay views; no placeholder proxy replaces authored meshes.

Upgrade choices use recognizable weapon/upgrade silhouettes, compact stat icons, truthful current-to-new values for no more than three decision-relevant deltas, restrained copy, and no NEW or LOCKED placeholder in the CURRENT column.
Upgrade cards expose complete keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus, hover, unavailable, newly-unlocked, and selected states without changing card dimensions.
Focused candidate checks pass for resource import/load, UI scene load, and deterministic Tester mesh/render/choice setup.
tasks.instructions: Repair authored visual/resource integration without destructive asset surgery. Trace the Bellkeeper and Grave Brute bindings, UV/material import settings, and wrapper/resource remaps that create degenerate UV surfaces; restore intact authored resources or correct product-owned bindings while preserving geometry, materials, textures, scale, and hierarchy in the native cemetery composition. In the same authored-presentation boundary, replace text-stacked weapon and upgrade choices with an authored visual hierarchy: silhouettes/icons lead each option, compact stat icons show only the few decision-relevant deltas, current-to-new values are truthful, unchanged/exhaustive rows are omitted, and keyboard/mouse/gamepad focus states are visually distinct. Do not substitute primitive, low-poly, matte, or placeholder enemy geometry, and do not use generic text-only cards. Leave deterministic mesh-validation, rendered-view, and upgrade-choice states for Tester recapture.
tasks.title: Repair authored meshes and upgrade-choice visual hierarchy

done_when: A single SEMI attack and a quick AUTO tap each produce exactly one short, recognizable lantern/firearm transient in mixed output, with no duplicate replay from generic VFX.
Player-world-surface impact audio is either a bounded, non-masking cue or explicitly disabled while compact impact VFX and character-hit feedback remain.

The retained component/player report path remains the sole owner; enemy spatial cues stay separate, sustained AUTO starts only after cadence-valid continuation, and release/lifecycle reset stops the cue.
Focused candidate checks pass for script/resource load and expose deterministic source-event/routing hooks for SEMI, AUTO, hit/miss, and lifecycle-reset Tester recapture.
tasks.instructions: Repair the automatic-combat audio integration around the existing retained weapon/component path. Use the adapter/material-impact envelope and routing as the root-cause boundary, not another generic presentation replay. Isolate player report, miss, concrete/metal/character hit, and enemy spatial stems. Ensure one SEMI click and one quick AUTO tap yield exactly one bounded recognizable transient, and prevent long ringing impact cues or generic shot VFX from masking/replaying it. If reliable world material tags cannot support a short surface cue, disable player world-surface impact audio while retaining compact impact VFX and character-hit feedback. Preserve existing weapon/component audio assets and hierarchy; enforce cadence-valid AUTO continuation plus stop-on-release and lifecycle reset. Leave source-event traces and adjacent event-window states for Tester to isolate mixed output and retest.
